reason: A cap keeps the talks honest, and the government is the only one with the money to pay for a fair rise.
Pay the rise nationally, but with a hard cap and a review date written in, so nobody can hide the bill.
Councils know their areas and their care homes. Give them a real say and some of the bill, or they'll just be told.
Local councils are closer to the money and the people. Keep it out of Whitehall and let them have a proper say.
The people who wash and feed my generation should be the ones signing off the deal, not a minister in London.
The government pays, but only up to a number we can see. Beyond that the talks have to find it, not the taxpayer.
Councils run the care in our area, so they should share the cost and have their say on the deal.
Workers and the people they look after should approve the deal. Parliament just pays for what they agree.
Care is a national job, so the nation should pay. But a cap and a review date are the sensible bit.
I want the pay rise to happen, and a fixed cap with a fixed end is the only way I trust it to last.
The government should pay, but with a ceiling written down. Otherwise the bill is open-ended and nobody can plan for it.
The people being cared for and the carers should have the last word. Parliament can sign the cheque after that.
